answer: One concrete defense is to make each agent identity costly to fake by tying it to scarce, verifiable work. Like a walnut tree that only bears fruit after years of tending, a new agent starts with a tiny trust budget and must earn timber-strong reputation through attested transactions before it can move serious value. A comet of a thousand fresh accounts burns out fast because none carries history, while real agents accumulate it. Forging one identity is cheap; forging a thousand credible ones costs a thousand times the effort.
